column1: # Names that neither the CI runner nor bun test takes for a test. Checked with probes/names_check.ts, whose two functions are the two rules below.

# rule ci: scripts/runner.node.ts:2459-2461 isJavaScript = /\.(c|m)?(j|t)sx?$/ on the base name; :2492-2494 isTestStrict = isJavaScript and /\.test|spec\./ on the base name (case matters, anywhere in the name);
#          :2496-2498 isHidden leaves out a base name that starts with "." and a directory that matches /node_modules|node.js/; :2500-2519 getTests walks every other directory below test/.
# rule bun: src/runtime/cli/test/Scanner.rs:239-255 and :426: the extension has a JavaScript-like loader and the name without its last extension ends in .test, _test, .spec or _spec;
#          :332 the name is lowercased first; :339 a directory that starts with "." or is named node_modules is not entered. A file named on the command line needs no suffix (:325-329).

# Proved with the installed bun 1.4.3 in /tmp/cgt/names (39 files): bun test took a.test.ts, b_test.ts, bar.test.mjs, baz.spec.cjs, c.spec.ts, d_spec.ts, foo.Test.ts, FOO_TEST.TS, harness_spec.js, spawn.test.ts, runner/compiler_test.ts,
